Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13                    Defendants.

                                  14

                                  15          On March 26, 2026, Plaintiff SLD Ecommerce, LLC (“SLD”) filed suit against Defendants

                                  16   PNC Bank, N.A. (“PNC”), Shopify, Inc. (“Shopify”), and Stripe, Inc. (“Stripe”), alleging claims

                                  17   for: (1) Breach of Contract; (2) Negligence; (3) Negligent Misrepresentation; (4) Breach of the

                                  18   Implied Duty of Good Faith and Fair Dealing; (5) Tortious Interference with Existing Business

                                  19   Relationships; (6) Tortious Interference with Existing and Prospective Business Relationships; (7)

                                  20   Declaratory Judgment; and (8) Injunctive Relief. Compl. at 1 (ECF No. 1). SLD asserts that the

                                  21   Court has jurisdiction over its claims based on federal diversity jurisdiction pursuant to 28 U.S.C.

                                  22   § 1332. Id. at 3. On June 17, 20226, SLD dismissed Shopify without prejudice. ECF No. 27.

                                  23          “Federal courts are courts of limited jurisdiction. They possess only that power authorized

                                  24   by Constitution and statute[.]” Kokkonen v. Guardian Life Ins. Co. of Am., 511 U.S. 375, 377

                                  25   (1994) (cleaned up). As such, they “have an independent obligation to ensure that they do not

                                  26   exceed the scope of their jurisdiction.” Henderson v. Shinseki, 562 U.S. 428, 434 (2011); see

                                  27   Valdez v. Allstate Ins. Co., 372 F.3d 1115, 1116 (9th Cir. 2004) (noting that district courts are

                                  28   “obligated to consider sua sponte whether [they] have subject matter jurisdiction”); Leeson v.
                                         Case 3:26-cv-02631-TSH            Document 28          Filed 06/18/26     Page 2 of 3




                                   1   Transamerica Disability Income Plan, 671 F.3d 969, 975 n.12 (9th Cir. 2012) (“Subject matter

                                   2   jurisdiction can never be forfeited or waived and federal courts have a continuing independent

                                   3   obligation to determine whether subject-matter jurisdiction exists.”) (cleaned up).

                                   4          There are two bases for federal subject matter jurisdiction: (1) federal question jurisdiction

                                   5   under 28 U.S.C. § 1331 and (2) diversity jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1332. A district court has

                                   6   federal question jurisdiction in “all civil actions arising under the Constitution, laws, or treaties of

                                   7   the United States.” 28 U.S.C. § 1331. A cause of action “arises under federal law only when the

                                   8   plaintiff’s well-pleaded complaint raises issues of federal law.” Hansen v. Blue Cross of Cal., 891

                                   9   F.2d 1384, 1386 (9th Cir. 1989). A district court has diversity jurisdiction “where the matter in

                                  10   controversy exceeds the sum or value of $75,000, . . . and is between citizens of different States,”

                                  11   or “citizens of a State and citizens or subjects of a foreign state . . . .” 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a)(1)–(2).

                                  12          Here, there is no federal question jurisdiction because SLD’s claims all arise under state
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   law. See Compl. at 1. In the Complaint, SLD avers that the Court has diversity jurisdiction under

                                  14   28 U.S.C. § 1332. Id. at 3. SLD alleges that it “is incorporated under the laws of the State of

                                  15   Wyoming and maintains its principal place of business at 30 N Gould St, Ste R, Sheridan, WY

                                  16   82801.” Id. at 2. SLD further alleges that complete diversity exists because SLD “is a citizen of

                                  17   Wyoming,” PNC “is a citizen of Pennsylvania,” Shopify “is a citizen of California,” and Stripe “is

                                  18   a citizen of California.” Id. at 3. As the party asserting diversity jurisdiction, SLD bears the

                                  19   burden of proving that diversity jurisdiction exists. See Resnik v. La Paz Guest Ranch, 289 F.2d

                                  20   814, 819 (9th Cir. 1961) (“[T]he burden of proving federal jurisdiction is upon the party asserting

                                  21   it[.]”) (citation omitted). “Generally, LLC’s are citizens of every state in which their

                                  22   owners/members are citizens.” Prairie Fire, LLC v. Van Vraken Enters., Inc., No. 13-cv-2772-

                                  23   JSC, 2013 WL 12149698, at *1 (N.D. Cal. Sept. 26, 2013) (citing Johnson v. Columbia Props.

                                  24   Anchorage, LP, 437 F.3d 894, 899 (9th Cir. 2006)) (cleaned up). Thus, SLD’s citizenship

                                  25   depends on the citizenship of its members and owners. However, SLD has failed to include any

                                  26   allegations as to the citizenship of its members and owners.

                                  27          Accordingly, SLD is ORDERED TO SHOW CAUSE as to the citizenship of any

                                  28   members or owners of SLD Ecommerce, LLC. SLD shall file a written response to this Order by
                                                                                           2

                                   2   jurisdiction.

                                   3           IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                   4

                                   5   Dated: June 18, 2026

                                   6
                                                                                                     THOMAS S. HIXSON
